Overview
Penguin Solutions is the AI Factory Platform Company. We design, build, deploy, and manage next-generation data centers for enterprises, sovereign AI initiatives, and neocloud providers.
With deep design expertise at the intersection of data center AI infrastructure and memory solutions, our Full-Stack AI Factory Platform combines differentiated infrastructure software, advanced memory, compute systems, end-to-end services, and industry-leading partner technologies to help customers accelerate deployment, optimize token economics, and maximize the return on their AI investments.
As of the end of fiscal 2026, Penguin Solutions employed approximatel y 2,800 employees worldwide, with most located in the United States, China, and Malaysia. We believe that our employee s are the cornerstone of our success. To support their efforts, we aim to provide inclusive and equitable workplaces maintained through ongoing intentional actions.
On October 15, 2024, we changed our corporate name from “SMART Global Holdings, Inc.” to “Penguin Solutions, Inc.” and changed our Nasdaq Global Select Market ticker symbol from “SGH” to “PENG.” The changes to the corporate name and ticker symbol did not have any impact on our legal entity structure, financial statements or previously reported financial information.
On June 30, 2025, we consummated the U.S. Domestication of the parent company of our corporate group from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware in the United States. For more information about the U.S. Domestication, see “About This Annual Report” above.
Business Segments
Penguin Solutions has three business segments: Advanced Computing, Integrated Memory, and Optimized LED. Each brings specialized expertise, innovative technologies, and a commitment to delivering high-quality products and services that meet evolving customer needs.
Our Advanced Computing and Integrated Memory businesses are central to our AI Factory Platform strategy, combining expertise in AI infrastructure, advanced memory technologies, and end-to-end services to help customers deploy, scale, and optimize next-generation AI data centers.
Our Optimized LED segment, operating as Cree LED, serves a distinct market with a dedicated strategy focused on advancing high-performance LED technologies and delivering innovative solutions to customers worldwide.
Divestiture of SMART Brazil
On November 29, 2023, we completed the divestiture of an 81% interest in SMART Modular Technologies do Brasil – Indústria e Comércio de Componentes Ltda. (“SMART Brazil”) to Lexar Europe B.V. (“Lexar Europe”), an affiliate of Shenzhen Longsys Electronics Co., Ltd. During 2026, we sold our remaining 19% interest in SMART Brazil, subsequently renamed Zilia Technologies, completing our divestiture of the business.
Presentation of SMART Brazil as Discontinued Operations: In accordance with authoritative guidance under U.S. GAAP, we have presented the balance sheets, results of operations and cash flows of SMART Brazil operations in this Annual Report, including in the accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes, as discontinued operations for all periods presented. The SMART Brazil operations were previously reported as part of our Integrated Memory segment. Unless otherwise noted, discussion within this Annual Report relates solely to our continuing operations and excludes the SMART Brazil operations. See “PART II – Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data – Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements – Divestiture of SMART Brazil” and “PART II – Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data – Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements – Cash and Investments – Non-marketable Equity Investments – Zilia Technologies.”
Our Products and Services
Advanced Computing
Our Advanced Computing segment delivers AI infrastructure solutions that help customers design, build, deploy, and manage next-generation AI data centers. Through our Full-Stack AI Factory Platform, we combine advanced compute systems, differentiated infrastructure software, and end-to-end services with industry-leading partner technologies to help enterprises, sovereign AI initiatives, and neocloud providers accelerate deployment, optimize performance, and improve token economics.
Our portfolio includes AI and high-performance computing (“HPC”) solutions offered under the Penguin Solutions ® and Penguin Computing ® brands, including our ClusterWareAI™ AI factory operating system software, MemoryAI™ data center and AI inference solutions, ComputeAI™ GPU and CPU computing systems, and OriginAI ® reference architectures. Our services span the AI infrastructure lifecycle, from design and deployment to ongoing optimization and managed operations.
We also offer high-availability and fault-tolerant computing solutions under our Stratus ® brand, supporting customers that require continuous availability and reliable operations in data center and edge environments.
Our Advanced Computing solutions serve enterprises, hyperscalers, sovereign AI initiatives, and neocloud providers. We help customers deploy and scale next-generation AI infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads.
Our Advanced Computing segment had net sales of $558.8 million, $648.4 million, and $554.6 million in 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
AI and HPC Data Centers
With more than 25 years of experience in AI and HPC infrastructure, Penguin Solutions designs, builds, deploys, and manages advanced computing environments that support demanding, data-intensive workloads. Our deep technical expertise and relationships with industry-leading compute, networking, storage, and software partners enable us to deliver scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure tailored to our customers’ needs.
Our Full-Stack AI Factory Platform combines OEM-like product innovation with system integrator-like end-to-end services and industry-leading partner technologies. Bringing together differentiated infrastructure software, advanced memory solutions, compute systems, and services, our platform helps enterprises, sovereign AI initiatives, and neocloud providers accelerate deployment, optimize performance, and scale AI infrastructure. As AI shifts toward inference-centric workloads and agentic AI, our integrated approach is designed to improve token economics and maximize the return on AI investments.
Our platform is built on five core elements:
OriginAI
OriginAI provides pre-validated AI infrastructure architectures designed to accelerate deployment and deliver predictable performance for GPU clusters ranging from hundreds to thousands of GPUs.
These architectures combine advanced compute, networking, storage, and software technologies with validated configurations to streamline infrastructure design, integration, and deployment. By reducing the time and effort required to configure and validate complex AI environments, OriginAI helps customers accelerate deployment, scale infrastructure efficiently, and achieve more predictable operational performance.
MemoryAI
Our MemoryAI portfolio is designed to address memory capacity, bandwidth, and efficiency challenges that increasingly constrain AI infrastructure performance, particularly for inference workloads. Our initial solutions focus on Compute Express Link or CXL-based memory technologies, including Key Value Cache memory expansion, to improve memory utilization and support more efficient inference operations. We are developing
additional capabilities intended to help customers improve GPU efficiency, optimize token economics, and maximize the return on their AI infrastructure investments.
ComputeAI
Our ComputeAI portfolio includes advanced compute systems designed to support demanding AI and HPC workloads. These systems provide the high-performance computing foundation for AI infrastructure, combining accelerated computing technologies with flexible system configurations to meet diverse workload and deployment requirements.
Our compute solutions support a broad range of applications, from traditional AI and HPC model training to increasingly demanding inference workloads. By integrating advanced processors, accelerators, memory, and networking technologies, ComputeAI enables customers to deploy and scale high-performance computing environments tailored to their operational needs.
ClusterWareAI
ClusterWareAI, our hardware-agnostic AI factory operating system software, provides centralized management, monitoring, automation and is designed to help optimize AI infrastructure. Its capabilities include cluster deployment, observability, GPU health monitoring, policy-based management, and automated remediation designed to help customers improve infrastructure reliability, operational efficiency, and GPU utilization.

Risk Factor Summary
The following summary is not exhaustive and should be read with the detailed risk factors and the other information in this Annual Report .
Risks Related to Our Business
• Changing worldwide economic conditions could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
• Our results of operations fluctuate from quarter to quarter, which makes them difficult to predict.
• We compete in historically cyclical markets.
• Fluctuations in average selling prices may have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• Tariffs or other trade restrictions or taxes have had in the past, and could have in the future, an adverse impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• We depend on a select number of customers for a significant portion of our revenue.
• Issues in the development of, our investment in, and use of AI or AI technologies, combined with an uncertain regulatory environment, may result in a material adverse impact on our business.
• The markets that we serve are highly competitive.
• We may be unable to optimally match purchasing and production to customer demand, which may have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• Our managed services engagements involve risks related to cost estimation, performance requirements and customer retention that could adversely affect our results of operations.
• Our future success depends on our ability to develop new products and services.
• Our customers often require that our products undergo a lengthy and expensive process of evaluation and qualification without any assurance of net sales.
• If our OEM customers decide to utilize standardized solutions instead of our specialty products, our net sales and market share may decline.
• We depend on a small number of sole or limited source suppliers.
• We may be unable to adapt to technological change or maintain or improve our manufacturing efficiency.
• Disruption of our operations at any one of our manufacturing facilities would substantially harm our business.
• We are subject to a number of procurement laws and regulations.
• Products that fail to meet specifications, are defective or that are otherwise incompatible with end uses could impose significant costs on us.
• Actual or perceived failures or breaches of our information and security systems, or those of our customers, suppliers or business partners, could expose us to losses.
• Actual or perceived non-compliance with applicable data privacy and security laws, or that of our customers, suppliers or business partners, could expose us to losses.
• Some of our offerings utilize open source software, which may pose particular risks to our proprietary software, products and services in a manner that could harm our business or make it easier for competitors to enter our markets and compete with us.
• Open source software may make it easier for competitors, some of which may have greater resources than we have, to enter our markets and compete with us.
• We could be prevented from selling or developing our software if our licenses are not enforceable or are modified so as to become incompatible with other open source licenses.
• Contracts with the U.S. Government may be terminated, cancelled or modified.
• Our indemnification obligations to our customers and suppliers could require us to pay substantial damages.
• We may need to raise additional funds, which may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.
• We have in the past made, and may in the future make, acquisitions, investments and/or alliances, which involve numerous risks.
• We may not achieve the intended benefits of the sale of our SMART Brazil business.
• We have incurred, and may in the future incur, impairment charges related to our goodwill, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• We may incur liabilities relating to additional Brazilian withholding tax in connection with the sale of our SMART Brazil business.
• If we are not able to maintain, develop and enhance our brand and our reputation, our business and results of operations may be adversely affected.
• We rely on third parties to sell a portion of our products and services.
• We may be unable to protect our intellectual property.
• Legal proceedings and claims could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• We may be required to pay royalties or obtain licenses to sell certain products.
• Changes in tax laws or potential adjustments by tax authorities could materially increase our tax expense, and our ability to use our tax attributes is limited.
• We have reversed valuation allowances for significant portions of our deferred tax assets, and we may not be able to realize these assets in the future. Our deferred tax assets may also be subject to additional valuation allowances, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
• We could incur substantial costs or liabilities as a result of violations of environmental laws.
• We may be unable to successfully manage environmental or social sustainability initiatives, in whole or in part, which could lead to less opportunity for us to have investors and partners and could negatively impact our reputation or options for capital acquisition.
• Our worldwide operations, and those of our suppliers, business partners and customers, may be disrupted by events outside of our control, including the effects of climate change, natural disasters, man-made disasters or other events, as well as societal and governmental responses to such events.
